questions.explanation: Discount is computed on the MARKED price, not on CP.

questions.question: In simple interest, the interest earned each year increases over time.
questions.explanation: Simple interest is FLAT — the same amount each year, computed on the original principal.

questions.question: The more frequent the compounding period, the larger the maturity amount.
questions.explanation: Half-yearly > yearly > 2-yearly compounding for the same r and t.

questions.question: For yearly compounding, the amount A = P · (1 + r/100)^____.
Express each as a percent: (i) 0.6, (ii) 3/4, (iii) 7/20.
questions.explanation: Decimal × 100 = percent; or fraction → decimal → percent.

questions.question: In a class of 80 students, 35 % play cricket and 25 % play football. How many play neither?
questions.answer: Cricket: 0.35 × 80 = 28. Football: 0.25 × 80 = 20. Total who play (assuming no overlap stated): 48. Neither: 80 − 48 = 32.
questions.explanation: Compute counts from percents; subtract from total. (Disjoint assumption used.)

questions.question: The price of a book rose from ₹240 to ₹300. Find the percentage increase.
questions.explanation: Always divide the change by the OLD value, then × 100.

questions.question: An article's price is increased by 20 % and then decreased by 15 %. Find the net percentage change.
questions.answer: Net factor = 1.20 × 0.85 = 1.02. So a 2 % NET increase.

questions.question: A trader buys 50 oranges for ₹150 and sells them at ₹4 each. Find the profit %.
questions.explanation: Lump-sum CP and SP across all units, then apply the profit-% formula.

questions.question: A washing machine is marked at ₹15000. After two successive discounts of 10 % and 5 %, what is the SP?
Find the simple interest on ₹6000 at 7.5 % p.a. for 2.5 years.

questions.explanation: Quarterly compounding uses A = P(1 + r/(100n))^(nt) with n = 4.

questions.question: Compare the maturity amount on ₹1000 at 10 % p.a. for 2 years under (i) simple interest, (ii) yearly compound interest.
questions.explanation: Same data; compounding adds the interest-on-interest piece.

questions.question: A trader sold an item for ₹720 at a loss of 10 %. At what price should he sell to gain 12.5 %?
questions.explanation: Two-step routine: recover CP from current SP and loss; then apply the new gain factor.

questions.question: The marked price of a watch is ₹2400. The shopkeeper offers a 25 % discount and still earns a 12.5 % profit. Find the cost price of the watch.
questions.explanation: Compute SP first (after discount); then back out CP using the gain factor.

questions.question: Mira deposits ₹20000 in a fixed deposit at 8 % p.a. compounded HALF-YEARLY. Find the maturity amount after 1.5 years and the compound interest earned.
questions.explanation: Half-yearly: half-year rate = r/2 = 4 %; number of periods = n · t = 3.

questions.question: Salt costs ₹40/kg. Its price first rose by 20 %, then fell by 10 %. Find (i) the new price per kg, (ii) the net percentage change from the original price.
questions.answer: (i) After 20 % rise: 40 · 1.20 = 48. After 10 % fall: 48 · 0.90 = 43.20. (ii) Change = 3.20; percentage change = (3.20/40) × 100 % = 8 % (an INCREASE). Or: (20 − 10 − 2) % = 8 % using the formula.
questions.explanation: Successive percentages multiply, not add. Use the (p + q + pq/100) shortcut to verify.
